title: Return to a Mid-Piacenzian Climate (Formerly Called the Middle Pliocene) Will Increasingly Spread Pathogens and Accelerate a Higher Severity of Pathogen Virulence by Immunogenomic Editing
content: A climate return to the mid-Piacenzian period (formerly called the middle Pliocene) is progressing with detrimental consequences, especially in the higher latitudes. This climatic shift is substantially increasing vector ranges geographically and increasing pathogen infections. This will additionally accelerate several evolutionary mechanisms that exist between pathogens, and the immune systems of subpopulations of vectors and hosts. Immunogenomic editing is defined as the evolution of pathogen genomes or the vector or host subpopulation immune system genomes. One immunogenomic editing classification, called immunoediting, was first recognized regarding cancer genomes. Two other immunogenomic editing classifications were subsequently recognized for pathogens and humans. However, these classifications of editing are only examples of much broader immunogenomic editing processes, and other potential classifications of immunogenomic editing were only recently recognized. Immunogenomic editing has at least seven potential classifications, and five immunogenomic editing classifications have applications including analysis of vector and host subpopulation pathogen responses. Additional benefits could also include facilitating analysis of subpopulation vulnerability differences to lethal pathogen epidemics. There are increased needs for quicker analysis of pathogen transmission chains and the immunogenomic mechanisms which enable quicker and broader transmission of dangerously virulent and lethal pathogens, since current transportation systems can quickly spread dangerous pathogens globally.
